opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
My husband and I have had two encounters with a church elder from the Jehovah's Witnesses congregation. He is a nice enough man. Sits at McDonald's and reads the scriptures. He is not shy to talk. He rattles off scripture as if it is within the context of everyday conversation.
Now my husband has always befriended the missionaries of the Jehovah's Witnesses congregation. They've come to our house often enough. He'll sit with them and talk it up. But recently we've learned they don't believe that Jesus Christ is divine. They believe he was created by God but don't consider him God. They refer to the Lord's prayer during the discourse, the part "hallowed be thy name". That is where Jehovah comes from as their first message. But there it stops. Of course, they believe in Jesus as his son, his first creation, but there it stops.
My husband does most of the talking; I never can dish it out sensibly. I have hiccups in my thoughts, but my heart listens. It is not that I am calling out or dismissing my fellow brethren, but I have not stopped thinking about this. Because I have so much to say but cannot form sentences. Because I guess I never quite understood what I believe, or at least the layers of belief that are there. Because there are many.
I dislike saying this, but we are superficial in our thoughts and prayers. Sometimes we go through the motion, think of when you say the Rosary. There are times when I am on the fifth mystery and not sure when I got there. But this, this interaction that has now happened twice, has me stuck.
Why? Well, it feels like blasphemy, I know that is a strong word. But our Jesus, the very son of God, died on a tree for Us. This cannot be overlooked. This very beautiful being secured our salvation, our ticket to the universe, Heaven. How can we deny that? How can we use the Bible to explain him away, when the very Bible itself is all about him. All the prophets that were ignored, whose very life purpose was to introduce him, to foretell him, to prepare the way for him.
Throughout the Gospel of John 6:52-59, "Unless you eat the Flesh of the Son of Man and drink his Blood, you do not have life within you". "Whoever eats my Flesh and drinks my Blood remains in me and I in him, says the Lord". This is spoken by God himself; that's it, it is done.
And our very Jesus says, "just as the living Father sent me and I have life because of the Father, so also the one who feeds on me will have life because of me".
If Jesus Christ is only created, how can His sacrifice fully reconcile all of humanity to God? Because Scripture does not speak of Him as partial or secondary, but as full.  In Gospel of John 1:1, we are told, “the Word was God.” Not near God, not like God—but was God. And that Word became flesh.
I'm sorry, I want to see all my brethren in heaven with me, celebrating our Holy God, our Mighty God, our Immortal God. I cannot stand to sit quietly with this. These interactions have made me steadfast in my belief, more so than ever.
This fellow's face is sweet, and he is doing God's work, but he cannot dissect the living Word with such conviction because he is leaving out the rest, and it is in the rest that is everlasting life.
Please, all of you, OPEN your hearts to the scriptures, pray to the Holy Spirit for his understanding and guidance, the more of us there are, the bigger the party.
